tasks.gr8-mineral-revolution-in-south-africa-t: Topic: The Mineral Revolution in South Africa. Cover gold mining, migrant labour, compounds, Johannesburg, land dispossession, segregation foundations, and the Union period. Ask Grade 8 learners to evaluate source snippets, identify cause-and-consequence links, sequence developments, and justify answers with evidence.
tasks.gr8-labour-control-and-land-t2: Topic: Britain, diamond mining and increasing control of labour and land. Cover closed compounds and migrant labour at Kimberley, and the further loss of land after the defeat of the Xhosa in 1878 and the Pedi and Zulu in 1879, including African resistance and the Zulu victory at Isandlwana. Ask Grade 8 learners to read short sources from different points of view, compare them, and explain cause and effect. Keep contested numbers out of questions.
tasks.gr8-gold-randlords-and-miners-t2: Topic: Deep-level gold mining on the Witwatersrand from 1886. Cover why gold is valuable, how deep-level gold is mined, conditions underground, the Randlords and the Chamber of Mines, migrant workers and the compound system, women in the reserves, skilled and unskilled white workers, anti-Indian legislation, forms of labour resistance and the growth of Johannesburg. Ask Grade 8 learners to read short sources from different points of view, compare them, and explain cause and effect. Keep contested numbers out of questions.
tasks.gr8-mineral-revolution-turning-point-t2: Topic: The Mineral Revolution as a turning point. Cover the defeat of the Boer republics in 1902, the African Political Organisation (1902), the Transvaal Indian Congress (1903), the Bambatha Rebellion (1906), Union (1910), the South African Native National Congress (1912), the Satyagraha campaign (1913 to 1914) and the Land Act (1913), and compare a map of 1913 with 1860. Ask Grade 8 learners to read short sources from different points of view, compare them, and explain cause and effect. Keep contested numbers out of questions.
